title: With `-flambda2-match-in-match`, a constant lifted from the toplevel code of a unit is left unwritten
summary: At `-O2` and `-O3` with `-flambda2-match-in-match` this program prints `result 0` instead of `result 2`: the block of `After delay_s` is a lifted constant whose field is never written. Whether it shows depends on the name of the file (keep `test.ml`); other programs end with a segmentation fault or stop the compiler. Issues #7763 and #7977 show the same fault with other programs (a stop of the compiler, and a segmentation fault).
cause: Each specialised copy of a handler in the toplevel code is simplified as toplevel code (`middle_end/flambda2/simplify/simplify_let_cont_expr.ml`), so a lifted constant waiting to be bound is bound inside the copy rebuilt first and used through the other.

fix.text: One line in `simplify_let_cont_expr.ml`: a specialised copy of a handler is simplified as not being at unit toplevel. Builds; `test.ml` then prints the expected result; testsuite unchanged. A compiler built with only this change also compiles and runs rightly the programs of issues #7763 and #7977. Regression tests exist and are not included here.
